title: Who decides who gets the hours?
caption:
A schedule decides a paycheck. The Daily Nun looked at who sets work schedules and what California law requires when a shift disappears.

A 2019 survey of about 30,000 workers at large retail and food chains found two-thirds got less than two weeks' notice. Rules on notice depend on the city.

reel.title: Who gets the hours?
reel.voiceover: Who decides who gets the hours? The employer does. A 2019 survey of thirty thousand workers at big chains found two in three got less than two weeks' notice. California sets a few limits. Sent home with under half a shift done? The worker is generally owed half the shift's pay. Under eighteen? Four hours, max, on a school day. The Daily Nun.
kineticText: Who decides who gets the hours?
Two in three: under two weeks' notice.
Sent home early? Some pay is owed.
Under 18? Four hours on school days.
The Daily Nun / A closer look at the world.

sources.title: It's About Time: How Work Schedule Instability Matters for Workers, Families, and Racial Inequality
sources.author: Daniel Schneider and Kristen Harknett
sources.publisher: The Shift Project, Harvard Kennedy School
sources.limits: About 30,000 employees at 120 of the largest U.S. retail and food-service firms; very large employers only; the brief does not break out high-school or student workers, and small businesses are not covered. Hardship findings are associations, not proof that schedules caused them. Read in full on 2026-11-15.

sources.title: Reporting time pay: frequently asked questions
sources.author: California Labor Commissioner's Office (DLSE)
sources.limits: Guidance, not the regulation itself (IWC wage orders, section 5). Has exceptions: threats, utility failures, acts of God, paid standby, shifts under two hours, and workers who leave on their own.

sources.title: Complying With Child Labor Laws: Information for Employers
sources.author: California Labor Commissioner's Office (DLSE)
sources.limits: Summary for employers. Exceptions exist, such as school-approved work experience programs. The statute (Labor Code section 1391) was not opened; the legislature's site blocked automated access.

sources.title: Fair Work Week Information
sources.author: City of Los Angeles, Office of Wage Standards
sources.limits: Applies only to retail employers with 300 or more employees globally, for work inside the City of Los Angeles. Other cities' rules were not checked.
